articles.title: 리콜 대상 김치냉장고서 ‘펑’…부산 사하구 아파트 화재
articles.snippet: 제품결함으로 리콜 대상이었던 김치냉장고가 폭발해 아파트 1가구가 불에 타는 사고가 발생했다.27일 부산소방재난본부에 따르면 전날 밤 9시 18분쯤 부산 사하구 소재 한 아파트에서 불이 났다.사고 당시 세대 거주자는 거실에서 TV를 시청하던 중 차단기가 내려가 이를 다시 올렸고 이후 ‘펑’하는 소리와 함께 김치냉장고가 있던 작은방이 검은 연기로 가득 찬 것을 확인했다. 이후 거주자는 승강기 앞에 설치된 옥내소화전으로 자체 진화를 시도했고, 주민 신고로 출동한 소방은 인원 45명과 장비 19대를 동원해 화재발생 10여 분만인 밤 9시 29분쯤 불씨를 완전히 잡았다.화재가 처음 발생한 김치냉장고는 2003년 제조된 제품으로 당시 리콜대상이었던 만큼 소방은 제품결함을 원인으로 추정하고 있다.화재로 2명이 대피했지만 인명피해는 없는 것으로 알려졌으며, 소방 추산 384만 원 상당의 재산피해가 발생했다.(부산=뉴스1)

Some dodgy episodes in his past, but still handles himself with style. In other words, Los Angeles personified is Cliff Booth – the over-the-hill stuntman played by Brad Pitt in Once Upon a Time … in Hollywood, now turned studio fixer in the sequel, The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth. Set eight years later in 1977, Further Mis-Adventures is more plot-driven, more Elmore Leonard-esque than the pure expansive “memory piece” of Once Upon a Time. But both films are steeped in the ambience and lore of old LA, drawn in part from Quentin Tarantino’s memories of cruising around the streets aged six in his stepdad’s Karmann Ghia (the car Booth also drives). They’re part of the recent intensely nostalgic LA revivalist mini-boom of work that also includes Paul Thomas Anderson’s Licorice Pizza (2021), Damien Chazelle’s Babylon (2022) and Ti West’s MaXXXine (2024). articles.title: ‘I was physically beating myself up before a take’: Rory Culkin on anxiety, fatherhood and his famous brothers
articles.snippet: The star of Lords of Chaos, Scream 4 and Gabriel was always drawn to the dark side. Is that why he seems happier in Hollywood than his better-known brothers – and why he loved making Nocturne with Stephen Graham? Rory Culkin is enjoying the autumn afternoon in a Manhattan park. The trees are a dazzling blur of yellows, greens, oranges and reds; the background silence is so pure you can hear it. “I’m here with my baby daughter, Havoc,” he says. “Havoc Moon.” I tell him that is the spookiest name ever. “Thank you,” he says. Culkin chuckles like a revving moped, his huge blue eyes lighting up. “Yes, it’s a weird one. I think she’ll probably be the opposite. A sweet, quiet girl. She’ll play a harp or something.” He explains its origin. “I just threw out names to my partner one night when we went to dinner. She wasn’t taking to anything. I then suggested Havoc, and she really liked it. She came up with the Moon part. When we got home there was fresh graffiti on the wall across the street saying ‘Havoc’, and I was like: ‘That is a sign from the gods – we’ve got to do it.’” Continue reading...

articles.title: Labour’s EU reset deal will be ‘floor not ceiling’, says Burnham cabinet ally
articles.snippet: Scottish secretary Douglas Alexander to say Britain cannot secure the change it needs ‘without changing our relationship with Europe’ Labour’s EU reset deal will be a “floor not a ceiling”, according to a close cabinet ally of Andy Burnham, who says the UK has been a “cork bobbing on the tides of history” because of the power lost by Brexit. Douglas Alexander, the Scottish secretary, will tell a conference in Italy on Friday that the government cannot deliver the major change Britain needs “without changing our relationship with Europe. When the status quo is not working, you don’t stand still. You move forward. When the status quo is broken, you don’t ignore it. You fix it.” Continue reading...

articles.title: Number of Neets in UK falls below a million as Burnham pushes to tackle crisis
articles.snippet: Latest figure of young people not in education, employment or training remains close to highest level in a decade Business live – latest updates UK politics live – latest updates The number of young people across the UK not in education, employment or training (Neet) has decreased but remains close to a million as Andy Burnham’s government pushes to tackle Britain’s youth jobs crisis. As ministers prepare to make sweeping changes in response to Alan Milburn’s landmark report on young people and work, the Office for National Statistics said the number of Neets fell by 22,000 in the three months to September, to 959,000. articles.title: Labour’s split over Rosebank oilfield exposed by letter from nearly 100 MPs
articles.snippet: Exclusive: Frontbenchers join scores of party colleagues urging Burnham not to let ministers approve project Opinion: Why Labour MPs are opposing Rosebank Podcast: are resignations next? Labour’s internal divisions over the giant Rosebank oilfield have spilled into the open, with nearly 100 Labour MPs – including a handful of frontbenchers – writing to the prime minister to express their opposition to the project. Ninety-two backbenchers and at least four frontbenchers have signed a letter to Andy Burnham urging him not to let his ministers approve the scheme for the biggest undeveloped field in UK waters. articles.title: Some old-school advice for Burnham: boost competition if you want growth | Nils Pratley
articles.snippet: Two former Treasury officials say the value of competition and disruption has become ‘the blind spot of UK economic policy’ The defenestration of Marcus Bokkerink in the Keir Starmer-Rachel Reeves era is half-forgotten now – but the saga was a big deal in January 2025 and should still matter to those at the top of today’s government. Bokkerink was chair of the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) until he was turfed out because, it seemed, he was deemed insufficiently aligned with the Starmer-Reeves idea that regulators should “support growth”. Bokkerink hit back by warning of the dangers of political interference and competition authorities becoming “vulnerable to short-term expediency or vested interests”. Continue reading...
